lane_status: The lane's first deliverable (shoreline elevation-versus-distance profiles with flagged steps) is already shipped by three earlier sessions on this repository (lane62/docs/downloads/lahontan_shoreline_profiles.json, 400 profiles; lane62-h62a). This session did not re-emit the datum geometry because the brief also requires a candidate that can beat the incumbent, and the datum band was measured BELOW chance on the only independent compilation (0.61x control, docs/research/leaderboard-arithmetic.md). The artifact below is emitted from a different, explicitly stated mechanism; the deviation is flagged here and in docs/irregularities.md.
hypothesis: The population the organizers define as new -- faults 'not included in the existing USGS fault database', explicitly including new geometry of existing systems (thread 11536) -- is best reached by the DERIVATIVE fields of the GeoDAWN stack plus metre-scale scarp evidence, because a lineament on the edge of a source body is a different (and sharper) object than the ridge of its potential, which is what the incumbent family filters. A k-of-N vote over independent physical families suppresses the single-layer confusers.
mechanism: 1) structure-tensor edge-line response L = sqrt(l1)*(l1-l2)/(l1+l2) at sigma = 1.2 px (120 m, i.e. matched to the metric's 300 m triangular kernel), computed for every band of the official 19-band stack (sha256 4371c82e..., byte-verified here), the radiometric and 3 m scarp products, the 10 m-derived topo stack and the 10 m channel-steepness stack; 2) per-layer rank transform, so each layer votes with its own top decile; 3) 13 derivative/ratio/steepness layers vote, weighted by the agreement of their doubled line directions; 4) a second, independent term is the metre-scale scarp evidence from the 1 m LiDAR composite (7 bands) and the 3 m scarp product (4 bands), gated by the vote; 5) score = 0.55*derivative_vote + 0.45*scarp_vote; 6) greedy top-score-first Poisson-disk emission with a hard 3 px (300 m) core, restricted to pixels >= 3 px off labels.tif; 7) write with gems62.grid.write_submission (re-reads the bytes) and re-validate.
named_non_fault_process_that_could_mimic: Fluvial and hillslope breaks: terrace risers, fan-head trenches, channel knickzones and gully edges all produce metre-scale linear steps, and the derivative fields respond to intrabasement magnetic/gravity contacts that are not faults at all. The k-of-N vote over independent families reduces but does not remove these; the 10 m channel-steepness layer in particular is expected to vote for knickpoints at lithologic contacts.

submission.name: gems62b-tiltgrad-vote-scarpcorrob-120000-zeros
submission.note_140: 62b: k-of-N vote over official-stack DERIVATIVE fields + 1m/3m scarp evidence, 120k dots hard-core 300m apart, off-catalogue. Diversity bet; no local instrument ranks it.

verdict_reason: Format-legal, provably isolated (max 1 dot per 300 m disk) and unique (max Jaccard 0.022, max tie-aware |rho| 0.035 against 25 prior rasters). It cannot be promoted as an expected improvement: its per-dot credit on the only positively-tracking local quantity is 0.0621, i.e. 95 % of the champion's 0.0655, and at 120,000 dots the published metric needs 0.0778 to beat 0.2778. The protocol's own promotion gate (HOLDOUT-DTI > 0.1322) FAILS at 0.00073, for the measured reason that the gate rewards catalogue-proximity while the leaderboard anti-rewards it (rho = -0.597, p = 0.0054, n = 20). Negative results are deliverables.
open_questions: No organizer-confirmed score exists anywhere in this repository; every comparison here is proxied. One receipt would convert the whole table.

The per-dot credit that would make this field beat 0.2778 (0.0778) cannot be measured locally: the two local instruments correlate +0.62 (credit/dot) and -0.44 (DTI and -0.60 (per-dot credit vs mapped catalogue) with the leaderboard, over 20 owner-reported scores.
